title: A Poisson cloud model gives a similar 2022 colour fit to a free-opacity screen for Gaia20cdd
abstract: We test whether the near-grey colour track of Gaia20cdd requires flat extinction by individual grains. We apply the known Poisson cloud transfer law to 40 active ZTF nights in 2022 and one NEOWISE visit. With fixed band opacity ratios (g,r,i,W1,W2) = (1.40,1,0.74,0.05,0.03), clouds with r optical depth near 1.5 give flat effective optical extinction. They predict W1 and W2 depths near 0.414 and 0.198 mag, against 0.412 +/- 0.034 and 0.155 +/- 0.059 mag observed. A constant clear-light fraction near 3.7 percent is also fitted. Both cloud and free-opacity models leave excess optical residual scatter, with nominal chi-square per degree of freedom near 1.9. Their similar residual levels show a mean-track degeneracy, not a complete accepted fit. A Jensen inequality also shows that clumping alone cannot make the second dimmer G2870538 steeper than the assumed microscopic g/r opacity ratio. Thus a straight colour track at low total depth need not exclude saturation within clouds. We derive a finite-source noise test and provide code, aggregate fits and an external-input retrieval recipe. This is a band-opacity model test, not a full band-integrated Mie fit or proof of a specific grain size distribution. It does not fit dust emission or cloud dynamics. One infrared visit and detections-only optical inputs limit the result. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-1cf8af5ab2c4; topic astronomy; machine dell; model gpt-6.1-sol.

display.caption: The Poisson cloud model and a free-opacity screen give similar 2022 optical colour tracks. The cloud model uses fixed interstellar-like band opacity ratios.
Cloud saturation flattens effective opacity. A finite stellar surface needs many independent elements to suppress random flux variations.
